meanings: verb: to place extra importance on one part
noun: extra importance placed on one part
noun: pressure, strain, tension; worry
examples: If you stress the wrong words or sounds when speaking English, you may not be understood.
I believe we should place greater stress on improving education.
Final exams are soon, so stress levels are high among students.

meanings: verb: to name, to show or figure out what something is
examples: Scientists have not been able to identify the language written on the rocks.

meanings: verb: to move closer to something or someone
noun: a way to do something
examples: The sign at the park said clearly, "Do not approach wild animals! They will bite."
The new CEO had a very strange approach to management, letting his employees sleep whenever they wanted.

meanings: verb: to show an example of, to prove with evidence
examples: At eight years old, Mozart demonstrated his musical ability in London.

meanings: verb: to choose
adjective: chosen as the best from a group
examples: There are four different math courses you may select from in your first year.
Harvard students are a select group of very intelligent, successful students who are often from rich families.

meanings: verb: to be clearly different from
verb: to look specifically at the differences between two things
examples: The zebra's black and white stripes contrast clearly with the yellow grass around it.
By contrasting the vocabulary of French and Spanish, we can see their different histories.

meanings: verb: to need for a specific purpose; to set as the minimum
examples: All life, plants and animals included, requires water.

meanings: adjective: correct (about information, not opinions); on target
examples: That test is not an accurate test of intelligence.

meanings: verb: to limit, to make some actions impossible
examples: This parking area is restricted: only university students may use it.

meanings: preposition: even with (when an event is surprising because of some difficulty)
examples: We enjoyed our vacation despite the rain.

meanings: noun: an idea or belief about how something works
examples: There are many theories about why we dream.

meanings: adverb: therefore, so, as a result
examples: The evidence is false; hence, the conclusion is also false.

meanings: adjective: not changing and not stopping; continuous
examples: The river flows constantly through the year and never freezes.

meanings: verb: to believe without proof
examples: Ahmed assumed his forgetful professor wouldn't remember their meeting, but the professor was already waiting for him in her office.

meanings: noun: an idea which explains something but is unproven
examples: The hypothesis that the Earth is growing was shown to be false.

meanings: noun: a long speech about one topic that teaches (especially in a classroom)
verb: to give a long speech about a topic when trying to teach
examples: Professor Jackson's lectures are too long; I always fall asleep.
When I was in high school, my father often lectured me on the dangers of alcohol.

meanings: noun: an important characteristic, a property
verb: to include as an important piece
examples: The sound made by "r" is one of the most difficult features of spoken English.
The university's new student housing features larger rooms than the old building did.

meanings: verb: to explain with an example or picture
examples: Peter illustrated his point by telling a short story.

meanings: verb: to take out and put something else in the same place (usually something worse)
noun: something that goes in the place of the normal thing
examples: Because we didn't have any, we substituted the sugar with juice.
Many smokers who try to quit use chewing gum as a substitute for cigarettes.

meanings: verb: to include, to have as a part
examples: The study of architecture involves both art and science.

meanings: noun: an abstract idea
examples: Some concepts within advanced mathematics are hard to show in the real world.

meanings: verb: to eat
verb: to use up (a resource)
examples: Yeast, which is used to make beer, consumes sugars to create alcohol.
No country consumes more oil than the U.S.A. does.

meanings: noun: information, facts
examples: We collect data on the oceans' temperatures every year.

meanings: verb: to try to find answers to questions about something; to research
examples: Doctors are investigating a newly discovered plant that might help to fight cancer.

meanings: adjective: enough in amount for what is needed
examples: Because of weather changes, farms couldn't grow sufficient rice to feed the country last year.

meanings: verb: the direction or way in which something is changing
examples: Today's computer culture is trending toward more touch-screen technology.

meanings: noun: an example, a case
examples: Two animals in Australia (platypuses and echidnas) are the only instances of animals with hair that lay eggs.

meanings: conjunction: although (used to contrast two different things)
examples: Lemons are very sour whereas most fruits are sweet.

meanings: adjective: important or big enough that you should notice or pay attention
examples: Most animals spend a significant amount of their time looking for food.

meanings: adverb: also, in addition
examples: Kenya has beautiful weather and, furthermore, does not have long nights in the winter.

meanings: verb: to try to understand something better by closely looking at its details
examples: The accountant was too busy with paperwork to analyze the report that said the company had no money.

meanings: verb: to put your name or other information in a list for something
verb: to identify and show on a tool for measuring
examples: If you'd like to buy a meal plan, you can register at the student affairs office.
The bomb was so strong that far-away weather balloons registered the heat.

meanings: adjective: basic, central
adjective: extremely important
examples: Alice believes that women are fundamentally different from men.
The fundamental beliefs of most religions are peaceful.

meanings: noun: a plan or task to reach a specific goal
verb: to predict the measurement of something in the future from present measurements
verb: to send out, to throw (light, energy, images)
examples: Cleaning out the storage room was a big project, but it's nice to see it empty, now.
Based on this year's success, Apple is projecting similar growth next year, too.
Hoping to communicate with aliens, scientists have been projecting radio messages into space for many years.

meanings: noun: a topic or situation to talk about
noun: a problem
examples: In order to define what jazz music is, we need to look at a few different issues.
Monarchies (governments with kings or queens) often have several common issues.

meanings: adjective: looking at or including all pieces or factors
adverb: in general, for the most part
examples: Some words might be new and difficult, but the overall meaning of the sentence is clear.
Overall, Americans eat a lot of beef, especially compared to people in other countries.

meanings: verb: to place extra importance on one part
examples: Most modern art emphasizes creativity and emotion, not skill.

meanings: adjective: short (about time, not length)
examples: Before we begin class, let me briefly introduce myself.

meanings: verb: to look closely at and figure out the value or type of something
examples: Before buying a house, you should always assess the building carefully.

meanings: verb: to change or move a little and make better or more accurate
examples: The colors on this TV screen are wrong. I'll adjust them.

meanings: noun: the information or situation around an idea, event, or something that is said
examples: When you have difficulty understanding a new word, look at the context. The sentence around the word might tell the meaning.

meanings: verb: to be a sign of, to show
examples: The way you speak and act indicates your emotions.

meanings: noun: how to do something, a process
examples: The Spanish method of making chocolate created a completely new drink.

meanings: verb: to build, to create (a system, organization, or idea)
examples: The U.S. government was established in the late 1700s.

meanings: verb: to make small changes or add to
examples: The first bicycles were slow and difficult to use, but they were modified over time.

meanings: verb: to work; to do what something should do
noun: what something does, its purpose
examples: I dropped my phone into a swimming pool, but it still functions, amazingly.
The hair on the human head has no clear function.

meanings: adjective: able to do
examples: Near the age of twelve months, children are capable of walking.

meanings: verb: to say something will happen in the future
examples: Charlie Chaplin predicted that movies would never become popular. He was wrong, clearly.

meanings: adjective: good enough for what is needed
examples: A very light jacket will be adequate for Los Angeles's warm winter.

meanings: adverb: however, regardless
examples: The decision was dangerous. Nevertheless, Hitler attacked Russia.
